mainTopic: Measuring the תחום from a desolate or inhabited city (שבת versus הניח עירוב), and the opening of chapter הדר: how a נכרי or a non-accepter of עירוב in a shared חצר forbids carrying.
overview: The גמרא opens with a dispute about a desolate city. שמואל says that according to the רבנן, one who is physically there when שבת begins may walk the whole city plus 2,000 אמות, but one who only placed his עירוב there gets just 2,000 אמות from the עירוב. רבי אלעזר says both may walk the whole city plus 2,000 אמות. The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר from the משנה's cave 'with no residents.' It answers that this means a place not fit to live in. A second challenge comes from a ברייתא that pairs a city with a cave. The גמרא answers by reading both places as inhabited and assigning the ברייתא to רבי עקיבא. The mention of מערת צדקיהו refers only to size. מר יהודה advises the people of מברכתא to place their עירוב deeper inside the shul, and רבא rejects this, because the הלכה does not follow רבי עקיבא. The chapter כיצד מעברין ends, and the new chapter's משנה rules that a נכרי, or one who does not accept עירוב, sharing a חצר forbids carrying there. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב limits this to a case with two Jews, and רבן גמליאל and רבי יהודה give two versions of a story about a צדוקי neighbor.

steps.title: שמואל: Being there versus placing an עירוב in a desolate city
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל. According to the רבנן, being physically present in a desolate city gives you the whole city plus 2,000 אמות. Placing an עירוב there gives only 2,000 אמות from the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If a person was in a desolate city when שבת began, then according to the רבנן he may walk through the entire city and 2,000 אמות beyond it. If he only placed his עירוב in a desolate city, he has only 2,000 אמות measured from the spot of his עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling from שמואל that separates two ways of setting your שבת 'home base' in a desolate city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you are physically in the city when שבת starts, the whole city counts like your four אמות, and your 2,000 אמות start from the city's edge. If you only placed an עירוב there, the city does not get that status, and you measure 2,000 אמות from the exact spot of the עירוב. So according to שמואל, the רבנן treat physical presence as stronger than an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A desolate city, one with no people living in it (its walls still standing)
He 'rested' there, meaning he was physically present at that place when שבת began
He placed his עירוב (food) there before שבת to make that spot his שבת home base
2,000 אמות, the standard שבת walking limit (תחום שבת)
He may walk through all of it, treating the whole city like four אמות

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean an עירוב is useless in a desolate city. It still works. The only question is where you start counting the 2,000 אמות: from the edge of the city, or from the exact spot of the עירוב.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one was present at the start of Shabbos in a desolate city,
according to the Rabbis, he may walk through all of it
and 2,000 amos outside it.
If he placed his eiruv in a desolate city,
he has, from the place of his eiruv,
only 2,000 amos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's discussion of measuring the תחום from a city or cave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, being physically present (שבת) in a desolate city gives the whole city plus 2,000 אמות. Placing an עירוב (הניח) gives only 2,000 אמות from the עירוב's spot.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: No difference between being there and placing an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees. Both the one who was present and the one who placed an עירוב may walk the whole desolate city plus 2,000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Whether he was physically there or he only placed his עירוב there, he may walk through the whole city and 2,000 אמות beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the opposing view: the method of setting your home base makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the desolate city counts as one unit whether you set your base by being there or by an עירוב. This erases שמואל's distinction. The rest of this passage tests רבי אלעזר's view against earlier sources.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, meaning the two cases are treated the same

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Whether he was present at Shabbos or he placed his eiruv,
he may walk through all of it
and 2,000 amos outside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמואל's distinction from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether present (שבת) or with an עירוב (הניח), one may walk the whole desolate city plus 2,000 אמות.

steps.title: Challenge from the cave case in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר from the משנה. The חכמים agree that someone who places his עירוב in a cave with no residents gets only 2,000 אמות. That seems to prove an empty place does not get the whole-city benefit when the base is set by an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי עקיבא said to the חכמים, 'Don't you agree with me that one who places his עירוב in a cave has only 2,000 אמות from the place of his עירוב?' They answered him: 'When is that true? When the cave has no residents.' So when it has no residents, they agree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exchange between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים in order to attack רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים admit that an עירוב placed in a cave with no residents gives only 2,000 אמות from the עירוב. A desolate city also has no residents. So when the base is set by an עירוב, it should likewise get only 2,000 אמות, just as שמואל said. That contradicts רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Akiva said to them:
Do you not agree with me
about one who places his eiruv in a cave,
that he has, from the place of his eiruv,
only 2,000 amos?
They said to him: When is that so?
When it has no residents.
So where it has no residents,
they agree with him?!
phrases.notes: This is the point of the attack: an empty place plus an עירוב means only 2,000 אמות, against רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's view from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that an עירוב in a desolate city gives the whole city plus 2,000 אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים agree that an עירוב in an uninhabited cave gives only 2,000 אמות. So an uninhabited (desolate) city with an עירוב should also give only 2,000 אמות.

steps.title: 'No residents' means not fit to live in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: 'no residents' means the place is not fit for living. A desolate city that is still livable keeps the whole-city status.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it has no residents' mean? It means the place is not fit for people to live in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by redefining the phrase 'no residents' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is a place that cannot be lived in at all, not one that just happens to be empty right now. A desolate city with standing walls is still fit for living. So even with an עירוב, it counts as one unit, and רבי אלעזר survives the challenge.
steps.whatToRemember: Two different things: 'empty right now' versus 'not livable at all.' Only a place that is not livable loses the whole-city benefit for an עירוב.

phrases.english: What does 'it has no residents' mean?
It is not fit for residence.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term (אוקימתא of the wording)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No residents' meant any empty place, which would include a desolate city.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No residents' means not livable at all. A livable desolate city still counts as one unit, even with an עירוב.

steps.title: A new source: a ברייתא about a huge city or a huge cave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. Someone who was in a city, even one as big as אנטיוכיא, or in a cave, even one as big as מערת צדקיהו, may walk all of it plus 2,000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If one was present at the start of שבת in a city, even one as large as אנטיוכיא, or in a cave, even one like מערת צדקיהו מלך יהודה, he may walk through all of it and 2,000 אמות beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second challenge to רבי אלעזר by first quoting a ברייתא. The attack itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that size does not matter: even a huge city or cave counts like four אמות. Notice that it speaks only of one who was present there (שבת). That detail is what the next step will use against רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Cave of צדקיהו, a famously enormous cave

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he was present at Shabbos in a city,
even if it is as large as Antioch,
or in a cave,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הִיא כִּמְעָרַת צִדְקִיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: even if it is like the Cave of Zedekiah, king of Judah,
he may walk through all of it
and 2,000 amos outside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second challenge to רבי אלעזר after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view, which treats the one who placed an עירוב the same as the one who was present.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's wording will be read closely in the next step.

steps.title: Inference: city is like cave, so only being there counts
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא pairs a city with a cave, and a cave is usually desolate, the city must be desolate too. And the ברייתא speaks only of being present, not of placing an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches 'city' together with 'cave.' Just as a cave is desolate, so too the city is desolate. And it says 'was present': yes, that works; but 'placed an עירוב': no, that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and draws an inference: the city is desolate, and only one who was present gets the whole-city benefit. This step sets up the attack. The next step completes it by showing that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pairing the city with a cave shows that the city in the ברייתא is a desolate one. The ברייתא grants the whole-city benefit only for 'שבת' (being present). That implies placing an עירוב in a desolate city would not get that benefit. This only hurts רבי אלעזר if the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and the next step proves that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes ... no (precise inference from the wording)

steps.whatToRemember: The inference from the ברייתא: a desolate city seems to give the whole-city benefit only to one who was physically present, not to one who placed an עירוב. Step 7 turns this into a challenge to רבי אלעזר, and Step 8 answers it.

phrases.english: It teaches 'city' similar to 'cave':
just as a cave is desolate,
so too the city is desolate.
And 'was present': yes,
but 'placed an eiruv': no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's equal treatment of שבת and הניח in a desolate city.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The city is like a cave, so it is desolate. The ruling is stated only for שבת. So הניח in a desolate city gets only 2,000 אמות, contradicting רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow the רבנן, which contradicts רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It cannot be רבי עקיבא, because then there would be no reason to mention a desolate city. So it must be the רבנן, and then the ברייתא implies that being present helps but placing an עירוב does not. That goes against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי עקיבא, why mention a desolate city specifically? The same would be true even of an inhabited one! So it must be the רבנן. And the reason he gets the whole city is that he was there for שבת. Yes, that works. But if he only placed an עירוב there, it does not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רבי אלעזר. It proves that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and that according to them an עירוב placed in a desolate city does not give the whole city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that someone who places an עירוב gets only 2,000 אמות from the עירוב even in an inhabited city. So if the ברייתא followed him, the desolate setting would add nothing. Therefore the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Under their view, the ברייתא's silence about placing an עירוב means placing one in a desolate city does not get the whole-city benefit, which goes against רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Whose view is it? If you say Rabbi Akiva,
why specifically a desolate city?
Even an inhabited one would be the same!
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא gives only 2,000 אמות from an עירוב even in an inhabited city.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the Rabbis?
And the reason is that he was there for Shabbat. Then, yes,
but if he only placed an eruv, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge built in Steps 5 and 6 by showing whose view the ברייתא follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that someone who places an עירוב in a desolate city gets the whole city
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא must follow the רבנן. It limits the whole-city benefit to someone who was present, so an עירוב placed in a desolate city gets only 2,000 אמות.

steps.title: Read it the other way: the cave is like the city, so both are inhabited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the comparison. The cave is like the city, so the cave is inhabited too. The ברייתא then follows רבי עקיבא, who limits an עירוב to 2,000 אמות but agrees that someone who was present gets the whole place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say the city is like the cave. Say the cave is like the city. Just as the city is inhabited, so too the cave is inhabited. And this follows רבי עקיבא, who said: a person gets only 2,000 אמות from the place of his עירוב. But if he was there for שבת, he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by reading the ברייתא differently. Both places are inhabited, and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 assumed the city was desolate, like a typical cave. Now the גמרא reverses that: the cave is inhabited, like a typical city. With both places inhabited, the 'present yes, placed no' contrast is רבי עקיבא's view. So the ברייתא says nothing about the רבנן and desolate cities, and רבי אלעזר is no longer contradicted.
steps.confusionAlert: Steps 6 and 8 use the same pairing of city and cave but read it in opposite directions. In Step 6 the cave 'leads', so both places are desolate. In Step 8 the city 'leads', so both places are inhabited.

phrases.english: Don't say the city is like the cave,
rather say the cave is like the city.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עִיר יְשִׁיבָה, אַף מְעָרָה יְשִׁיבָה.
phrases.english: Just as the city is inhabited, so too the cave is inhabited.
And it follows Rabbi Akiva, who said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ מִמְּקוֹם עֵירוּבוֹ אֶלָּא אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה,
phrases.english: he has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eruv,
but if he was there for Shabbat, he agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא עִיר דּוּמְיָא דִמְעָרָה, אֶלָּא אֵימָא מְעָרָה דּוּמְיָא דְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 6 and 7 by reversing the direction of the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the comparison is reversed and the ברייתא is assigned to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The city is like the cave, so both are desolate, and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cave is like the city, so both are inhabited, and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא. רבי אלעזר is not contradicted.

steps.title: But the ברייתא mentions מערת צדקיהו, which was desolate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. The ברייתא names מערת צדקיהו, and that cave was not inhabited.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'like מערת צדקיהו'! That cave was desolate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8. The cave the ברייתא mentions by name was desolate, so how can the ברייתא be about an inhabited cave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 needs the cave to be inhabited. But the ברייתא uses מערת צדקיהו as its example, and that cave was empty. That seems to show the ברייתא is about a desolate cave after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Cave of צדקיהו, a huge cave with no residents

phrases.english: But it teaches 'like the Cave of Zedekiah'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 8 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 8 that the cave in the ברייתא is inhabited
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own example, מערת צדקיהו, was a desolate cave.

steps.title: Like מערת צדקיהו only in size, not in being empty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares the cave to מערת צדקיהו only in how large it is. Unlike that cave, this one is inhabited.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like מערת צדקיהו, and not like מערת צדקיהו. It is like מערת צדקיהו in being large. It is not like מערת צדקיהו because that one was desolate, and here it is inhabited.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The comparison to מערת צדקיהו is only about size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the name only to show how big a cave can be and still count as one place. It does not mean the cave was empty. So the reading in Step 8 holds: the ברייתא is about an inhabited cave and follows רבי עקיבא, and רבי אלעזר is saved.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר survives. The ברייתא of אנטיוכיא and מערת צדקיהו is about inhabited places and follows רבי עקיבא. The mention of מערת צדקיהו is only about size.

phrases.english: Like the Cave of Zedekiah, and not like the Cave of Zedekiah.
Like the Cave of Zedekiah in being large.
And not like the Cave of Zedekiah:
because there it was desolate, and here it is inhabited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9 by limiting what the comparison covers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison: it is only about size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming מערת צדקיהו means the cave is desolate.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name only shows the size. The cave in the ברייתא is inhabited.

steps.title: מר יהודה tells the people of מברכתא to place their עירוב deeper inside
steps.stepSummary: מר יהודה saw the people of מברכתא placing their עירוב in the shul of בי אגובר. He told them to put it farther in, so they would be allowed to walk farther.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר יהודה found the people of מברכתא placing their עירובין in the shul of בי אגובר. He said to them: Put it farther in, so that more will be permitted to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a practical story. It shows a rabbi teaching people how to place their עירוב to gain the most walking distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר יהודה holds that the 2,000 אמות are counted from the exact spot of the עירוב, even in an inhabited town. So moving the עירוב farther in, in the direction they want to walk, moves their whole limit forward. That is רבי עקיבא's view from Step 8, and the next step objects to it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that, by this view, the exact spot of an עירוב matters, because the walking limit is counted from that spot.

phrases.english: Mar Yehuda found the people of Mavrakhta
placing their eruvin
in the synagogue of Beit Agovar.
He said to them: Place it farther inside,
so that more will be permitted to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over the ברייתא to a practical story about where an עירוב should be placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 2,000 אמות are measured from the spot of the עירוב, so placing it farther in gains more walking distance.

steps.title: רבא rejects מר יהודה's advice
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells מר יהודה that the הלכה in עירובין does not follow רבי עקיבא, so where the עירוב sits inside the town makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: "Argumentative one! When it comes to the laws of עירוב, nobody pays attention to this view of רבי עקיבא."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against what מר יהודה told the people of מברכתא in Step 11. He says the reasoning behind that advice is not the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר יהודה's advice only makes sense according to רבי עקיבא, who measures 2,000 אמות from the exact spot of the עירוב. The הלכה follows the רבנן, who treat the whole town as if it were just four אמות. So no matter where the עירוב is placed inside the town, a person may walk 2,000 אמות past the town's edge.

keyTerms.meaning: Argumentative one; someone who takes a minority or opposing position
Nobody is concerned about this; nobody follows it
The laws of עירוב, here meaning עירובי תחומין

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה follows the רבנן: a person whose עירוב is anywhere inside an inhabited town counts the whole town as four אמות and walks 2,000 אמות beyond it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the long discussion about a town and a cave. In practice, the exact placement of an עירוב within a town makes no difference.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: Argumentative one!
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking to מר יהודה.

phrases.english: With regard to eiruv, nobody is concerned
phrases.notes: Nobody rules this way in practice.

phrases.english: about this view of Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: His view is that the 2,000 אמות are measured from the עירוב itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical instruction that מר יהודה gave in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The practical advice to move the עירוב deeper into the shul
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The advice assumes רבי עקיבא's view, but the הלכה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter כיצד מעברין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter כיצד מעברין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כיצד מעברין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line signals that the chapter about measuring town borders and תחומין has ended. The next line begins a brand-new chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell to a finished chapter, expressing the hope to learn it again. No new argument or law appears here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula for finishing a chapter
"How do we extend [town borders]"; the name of the chapter that is ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, "How do we extend"
phrases.notes: This is the end of the fifth chapter of עירובין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter whose last discussion ended in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter on extending town borders and measuring תחומין is complete.

steps.title: A neighbor who does not join the עירוב prevents carrying
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that someone who lives in a shared חצר with a נכרי, or with a person who does not accept עירוב, is forbidden to carry there.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person lives in a courtyard together with a נכרי, or with someone who does not accept the idea of עירוב, that neighbor makes it forbidden for him to carry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a basic rule about עירובי חצרות. Some neighbors cannot join the עירוב, and their presence blocks everyone else from carrying in the shared חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying between houses and a shared חצר normally needs an עירוב that includes every resident. A נכרי cannot join the עירוב, and neither can someone who rejects עירוב entirely, such as a כותי. Since they still have rights in the חצר, they make carrying forbidden. The גמרא later explains that the solution is to rent their rights.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard shared by several houses
Someone who accepts the concept of עירוב
Makes it forbidden, here meaning forbidden to carry

steps.confusionAlert: "Forbidden" here does not mean the Jew may not live there. It means he may not carry between his house and the shared חצר on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who lives with a gentile in a courtyard,
phrases.notes: This is the opening of the new chapter, הדר.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עִם מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָּעֵירוּב
phrases.english: or with one who does not accept the eiruv,
phrases.notes: For example, a כותי or a צדוקי.

phrases.english: this person renders it forbidden for him.
phrases.notes: The Jew may not carry between his house and the חצר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter and topic after the הדרן in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי, or someone who does not accept עירוב, living in a shared חצר forbids a Jew from carrying there.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires two Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argues that the נכרי forbids carrying only when at least two Jews live in the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The נכרי never makes it forbidden unless there are two Jews living there who would forbid carrying for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with the first rule of the משנה. He narrows the case where a נכרי blocks carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, a single Jew living alone with a נכרי may carry. The נכרי only causes a problem when there are already two Jews who would need an עירוב with each other. In that case, the נכרי's presence keeps their עירוב from working.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbid carrying for each other

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says even one Jew is restricted by the נכרי. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only two or more Jews are restricted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
Actually, he does not render it forbidden
unless there are two Jews
who forbid carrying for one another.
phrases.notes: Without an עירוב, they would restrict each other anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes and narrows the first opinion of the משנה in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי forbids carrying only when two or more Jews share the חצר.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's story about the צדוקי neighbor
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells of a צדוקי in their מבוי in ירושלים. His father told them to hurry and bring their utensils out into the מבוי before the צדוקי brought his out and made it forbidden for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: There was a story with a צדוקי who lived with us in an alleyway in ירושלים. Father said to us: Hurry and take the utensils out into the alleyway, before he takes his out and makes it forbidden for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real-life story from רבן גמליאל to show how the rules of sharing a space with a non-accepter of עירוב actually played out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צדוקי does not accept the Rabbis' idea of עירוב, so he is like the 'one who does not accept עירוב' from the משנה. In this story the צדוקי had given up his rights in the alleyway before שבת. The father told them to quickly take their utensils out and establish their use of the alleyway, before the צדוקי changed his mind, took his own things out, reclaimed his rights and forbade the alleyway to them.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sadducee — someone who rejects the Oral Torah and Rabbinic laws like עירוב
An alleyway that several courtyards open into
A story or incident that happened
Take the utensils out — use the space to claim it
He will make it forbidden for you

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here is רבן גמליאל's father, not a generic 'father'. Also, in רבן גמליאל's version the צדוקי is not treated as a נכרי (רבי יהודה's version in the next step may differ); the question in this story is how his rights in the alleyway work.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
There was an incident with a certain Sadducee
who lived with us
in an alleyway in Jerusalem,
and Father said to us:
Hurry and take the utensils out into the alleyway,
phrases.notes: Claim the space by using it first.

phrases.english: before he takes his out and makes it forbidden for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּצַדּוּקִי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the משנה's rule about living with one who does not accept עירוב, using a real incident.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a צדוקי neighbor has given up his rights in the alleyway, the Jews should quickly take their utensils out to establish their use of it, before he takes back his rights and forbids it to them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's different version of the father's words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports the father's words differently: Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway before he takes out his things and forbids it to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The father said it in different words: Hurry and do whatever you need in the alleyway, before he takes his things out and makes it forbidden for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees about how the story went. He gives his own version of what רבן גמליאל's father told them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version the father does not say 'bring out the utensils.' He says 'do what you need,' which means getting everything done before שבת. This suggests רבי יהודה holds that a צדוקי cannot give up his rights like a Jew, so with him the alleyway cannot be used at all on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: In different words — a different version of the quote
Do what you need (take care of your needs)

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions are not just a style difference. Changing 'take out the utensils' to 'do what you need' changes the law: one allows using the alleyway on שבת, the other implies finishing everything before שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whether a צדוקי is treated like a Jew, who can give up his rights in the alleyway, or like a נכרי, who cannot.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל: rush to claim the alleyway with utensils, so it can be used. רבי יהודה: rush to finish your needs before שבת, because the צדוקי will make it forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
with a different wording —
Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway,
before he takes out his things and makes it forbidden for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of the quote in step 16, which carries a different halachic meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי יהודה, the father told them to finish their needs in the alleyway before שבת, implying the צדוקי's presence forbids carrying there on שבת.
